results.response:
Here's what I found:

Level 1 charging uses a standard 120V household outlet and adds approximately 3-5 miles of range per hour. Level 2 charging requires a 240V circuit (typically installed by an electrician) and adds approximately 20-30 miles of range per hour depending on onboard charger capacity. For daily commuting, Level 2 home charging overnight is sufficient for most driving patterns. (Source: Owner's Manual — Charging — Level 1 and Level 2)

DC fast charging can restore 10%-80% state of charge in approximately 30-40 minutes under optimal conditions. Charging speed slows significantly above 80% to protect battery longevity, so fast charging is most time-efficient when used for the 10%-80% range rather than charging to 100%. Battery preconditioning (automatically triggered when a fast charger is set as the navigation destination) improves charging speed in cold weather. (Source: Owner's Manual — Charging — DC Fast Charging)

results.response:
Here's what I found:

For daily use, keeping the battery between 20% and 80% state of charge maximizes long-term battery health. Charging to 100% is recommended only before long trips. Battery degradation of 5-10% over 8 years or 100,000 miles is typical and covered under the battery warranty if it falls outside expected ranges. (Source: Owner's Manual — Battery Health and Longevity)

The high-voltage battery and drive unit are covered for 8 years or 120,000 miles, whichever comes first, against defects and against capacity falling below 70% of original rated capacity. The comprehensive vehicle warranty covers 4 years or 50,000 miles. Wear items (tires, wiper blades, brake pads) are not covered under warranty. (Source: Warranty Guide — Battery and Drive Unit Warranty)
